thread:
sasha: Heads-up — eu-west dedicated pool A is spiking p99 token latency (~800ms) for the last 6m. NIC err_rate on a couple hosts is elevated. Suspect a noisy tenant or NIC saturation.
infra-bot: ALERT: DedicatedPoolA p99=820ms, affected slices: slice-az3-[12,13]. NIC errs: eth0 drops=4120, tx_errors=38. Incident created INC-2026-348.
sasha: tagging infra team — any immediate ideas? want to avoid full pool drain if possible.
kevin: saw kernel drop counters rising on those hosts + nvlink drop warnings in dmesg. Not purely CPU. Could be a tenant doing huge concurrent memcpy patterns.
ana: (typo) ana: can we soft-quarantine the tenant? moving to fallback dedicated pool will cost double for a bit but should cut cross-talk.
sam: propose micro-quarantine flow: 1) apply egress cap 2) pin offending tenant to isolated slice (if available) 3) force kv-cache regen for other tenants. Minimal disruption.
maria: command to limit egress quickly: `routeset apply --tenant t-4321 --egress-bandwidth 10mbps --reason "micro-quarantine"`
kevin: +1 to bandwidth cap. also set NIC tx queue max to 1000 for that slice to throttle bursts.
sasha: can infra-bot run the bandwidth rule? I don't have perms from mobile.
infra-bot: I can stage a job but need an approver. Approvers: @kevin, @maria.
kevin: approving now. running staged job.
kevin: job started: `quarantine-run 3612349876 --tenant t-4321 --caps egress=10mbps queue=1000 --duration 600`
sam: after applying cap, watch p99 across pool — expecting fall to ~50ms if noisy neighbor is root cause.
kevin: update — p99 dropped to 48ms within 90s, NIC errs trending down. Looks promising.
ana: (ana): CS heads-up? customer may see throttling. We should message them before longer quarantine.
maria: short comms draft: "We're investigating intermittent latency in eu-west dedicated pool; to protect overall performance we've temporarily limited network bursts for a small set of workloads. We're monitoring and will follow up." ok?
sasha: yep send that. Sam/kevin, can you capture logs for postmortem: `ethtool -S`, `dmesg | tail -n 200`, and router counters.
sam: done — pasted gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/egress-quarantine-3612349876
kevin: also captured perf trace of memcpy syscalls — heavy GPU->host memcpy cadence. Attaching sample: `memcpy_samples.log` (uploaded).
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-348 updated: mitigation applied (egress cap + slice pin), state=mitigating.
sasha: action items: - temporary quarantine window 10m (we can extend) - run targeted stress test to reproduce - schedule firmware driver check on affected hosts in next maintenance window - PM to own postmortem
maria: stress test command for repro: `wrk -t8 -c200 --duration 120s http://slice-az3-proxy/healthz` (simulate burst connections).
sam: ran stress test in canary — no regression. p99 stable.
kevin: recommend a weekly scan to detect memcpy-heavy tenants and flag them for soft-quarantine preemptively. Could be automated heuristic (nic errs + p99 > 300ms).
nana: +1. also add CS notif template to runbook so customers aren't surprised.
sasha: agreed. I'll draft runbook changes after I finish incident notes. Will leave quarantine for another 15m and then progressively relax caps.
kevin: thanks all. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-348 will be auto-resolved if p99 stays <100ms for 30m.
sasha: resolving thread — follow-up postmortem in #postmortems.
